points.t: **Comedones** (the hallmark) with papules and pustules on face, chest and back.
12-week fixed-combination topical; add an oral tetracycline if moderate–severe. Never antibiotic alone.
Acne fulminans (unwell, ulcerating): same-day dermatology. Scarring or distress: refer early.

cause.lead: Four factors acting in one hair follicle.
points: **Inflammation** turns comedones into papules, pustules and nodules.
**Aggravators**: PCOS, comedogenic cosmetics, picking, steroids, lithium, EGFR inhibitors. Diet: NICE finds insufficient evidence.

visuals.caption: One follicle, five stages (left to right): normal → closed comedone → open comedone → inflamed papule-pustule → deep nodule.
visuals.alt: Five cross-sections of a hair follicle progressing from normal to nodule

points: **Sites**: face, neck, upper chest, back, shoulders.
**Sequelae**: post-inflammatory erythema or pigment; ice-pick, rolling, boxcar scars.

visuals.caption: Where acne appears: face, central chest, upper back and shoulders. Trunk involvement shapes treatment choice.
visuals.alt: Face, chest and back outlines dotted with acne lesions

items.name: Open comedones
items.t: Dilated follicles with dark keratin plugs.

items.name: Closed comedones
items.t: Small skin-coloured papules; use side lighting.

items.name: Papulopustular
items.t: Inflamed papules and pustules with comedones.

items.name: Nodulocystic
items.t: Deep nodules and cysts with scarring: refer.

items.name: Truncal
items.t: Papules, pustules, nodules on back and chest.

items.name: Pigment change
items.t: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, often the main worry.

points: Duration; past treatments, how long, adherence.

scale.t: Any of: comedones; ≤ 34 inflammatory lesions; ≤ 2 nodules

points: Hormone profile if atypical or hyperandrogenism.

cards.name: Rosacea
cards.clue: Central flushing, telangiectasia, **no comedones**; usually older.

cards.name: Perioral dermatitis
cards.clue: Papules round mouth and eyes, sparing the lip border; often steroid-triggered.

cards.name: Folliculitis
cards.clue: Follicular pustules, often truncal; no comedones.

cards.name: Milia
cards.clue: Tiny white keratin cysts; not inflamed.

manage.lead: NICE NG198. Offer one 12-week option after shared decision-making.

points: Syndet cleanser twice daily; no scrubbing.
OTC **benzoyl peroxide** while waiting. Results take **6–8 weeks**.

rx.note: With adapalene + BPO, or azelaic acid 15–20% BD.
Same partners. Tetracyclines unsuitable: trimethoprim or a macrolide (NG198).

points: Consultant-led team only, under **MHRA** measures and the **Pregnancy Prevention Programme**.
Mental health and sexual function counselling; LFT and lipids.

limits.t: Topical or oral antibiotic alone, or both antibiotics together.
Stop the oral antibiotic once clear; keep the topical.
Antibiotic regimens beyond 6 months only exceptionally, with 3-monthly review.

sites.t: Adapalene + BPO, or adapalene, azelaic acid or BPO alone.
BPO alone if avoiding a retinoid or antibiotic.
No tetracyclines (intracranial hypertension), no vitamin A; POP not enough for the PPP; 30-day supply, dispense within 7 days.

items.t: Low mood or suicidal thoughts: assess and escalate, especially on isotretinoin.
Acne conglobata, nodulocystic acne, or diagnostic doubt.
Mild–moderate failing **two** courses; moderate–severe failing a regimen with an oral antibiotic.
**Scarring**, persistent pigment change or significant distress, at any severity.

pearls.t: Start topicals on **alternate days** or short-contact, then build up.
**Pregnancy**: no topical retinoids or tetracyclines. BPO ± clindamycin with caution.
Combined pill preferred over POP; co-cyprindiol in selected women (VTE risk, review ~6 months).
Depression is common with acne itself: screen regardless of drug.

quiz.q: Which lesion is the hallmark that separates acne from rosacea?
Name the three antibiotic rules in NG198.
quiz.a: Never a topical antibiotic alone, never an oral antibiotic alone, never topical + oral antibiotic together.

quiz.q: When do you review a 12-week course?
quiz.a: At 12 weeks. Stop the oral antibiotic once clear and continue the topical.

quiz.q: Which acne presentation needs same-day referral?
Why are tetracyclines and isotretinoin never combined?
